svg.title: The Reseller Tax Setup
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-resale-tax-setup; chapter number: 11; title: The Reseller Tax Setup; subtitle: One seller's permit at the hub, certificates and filings on every spoke; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Reseller holding a seller's permit; headcount: Owner-operator; focus: Collect and remit sales tax, and buy inventory tax-free so the tax lands once, on the end consumer.; spokes: role: Florida Department of Revenue (DR-1 and DR-13); type: Registration and renewal; kpi: DR-13 pushed to every vendor before December 31; quarterly return filed even at zero in-state sales; role: Out-of-state vendors (SST and MTC forms); type: Multistate exemption; kpi: 35 of 45 sales-tax states covered; about 10 states require registration; role: Retailers and online sellers; type: Point-of-sale exemption; kpi: About 50 printed certificate copies a year; yes-list retailers only; role: Certificate misuse guardrail; type: Audit exposure; kpi: Tax due plus 10% of the tax or $500, whichever is more, per misused purchase; caption: Skipping the certificate means paying $70,000 on $1,000,000 of inventory at 7%; in Florida, wholesale buys run 7% to 7.5% once county surtax is added.; assumptions note: State rules shown are the practitioners' reported examples for Florida and California and vary by state.; note: Attributed to James Baker CPA (CiHy9lcx3x4, L4NQWUrzH6A), Santiago Cueto (K5oBesJVonE), LedgerGurus (It-VnUi3x58), Lester John (7J3W8esngfU), Jack Hagwell (iNfW7YXuTOA), and Matt Sokol Business (vwdB1U0_hGs).
